Bear Story

Winnie-the-Pooh turns 100 this year. People of all ages love the willy-nilly silly old bear. You might know him from a cartoon. He is a yellow bear in a little red shirt. He is often found in a jar of “hunny.” Before he was on a screen, he was in a book.

Winnie-the-Pooh was published in 1926. The book was written by A.A. Milne. It was illustrated by Ernest H. Shepard. Learn how this beloved bear came to be.

Christopher Robin’s Pal

Christopher Robin is a character in Winnie-the-Pooh. He is based on Milne’s son, Christopher. Christopher had a stuffed bear. Its name was Mr. Edward Bear. Then Christopher saw a bear in the London Zoo. Its name was Winnipeg. Christopher renamed his bear Winnie. The name Pooh came from a pet swan.

Christopher loved his bear. He asked his dad to tell him stories about it. His father turned the stories into books. They are set in a real place. The Hundred Acre Wood is based on Ashdown Forest. It is in England.

Pooh and Friends

Milne’s stories of Pooh and friends grew very popular. In 1966, Walt Disney had the characters animated. They were put into a short. The characters have been on screens and in kids’ bedrooms ever since.

People can see Christopher’s original stuffed animals. They live at the New York Public Library (NYPL). Brent Reidy is a director of research libraries at NYPL. He says the display celebrates Winnie-the-Pooh and Milne. They have had the “ability to charm readers for 100 years,” he says, “and counting.”
